a-baby-in-a-basket-for-kids.q: Why did Pharaoh order all Hebrew baby boys to be thrown into the Nile?
options: He wanted to make room in the hospitals
He was afraid the Israelites were becoming too many and too powerful
He wanted to punish Moses specifically
a-baby-in-a-basket-for-kids.why: Pharaoh saw that the Israelites kept growing in number and he feared they might rise up against him, so he cruelly ordered all newborn Hebrew boys to be killed.

a-baby-in-a-basket-for-kids.q: What did Moses' mother do to save him?
options: She disguised him as an Egyptian baby
She sent him on a ship to another country
She placed him in a waterproof basket among the reeds of the Nile
She hid him in a cave in the mountains
a-baby-in-a-basket-for-kids.why: After hiding Moses for three months, his mother made a basket, coated it with tar and pitch to make it waterproof, and placed him among the reeds of the Nile River.

a-baby-in-a-basket-for-kids.q: What amazing thing happened after Pharaoh's daughter found baby Moses?
options: Moses' own mother was hired to nurse and raise him
He was sent to live with another Hebrew family
a-baby-in-a-basket-for-kids.why: Miriam cleverly offered to find a Hebrew woman to nurse the baby, and she brought Moses' own mother -- who then got paid by Pharaoh's daughter to raise her own son!

a-new-creation-for-kids.q: According to 2 Corinthians 5:17, what happens when someone is "in Christ"?
options: They become a slightly better version of themselves
They have to earn their way to a new life
The new creation has come — the old has gone, the new is here
They stay the same but try harder
a-new-creation-for-kids.why: Paul says it clearly — if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come. The old is gone. The new is here. You're not just improved — you're completely new, like a caterpillar becoming a butterfly.

a-new-creation-for-kids.q: What did Paul mean when he said, "I have been crucified with Christ"?
options: Paul was literally on the cross with Jesus
The old version of himself — controlled by sin and selfishness — died with Jesus, and a new life began
Paul was punished for his past mistakes
He had to give up everything he owned
a-new-creation-for-kids.why: Paul meant that his old self — the person controlled by fear, shame, and sin — went to the cross with Jesus. And when Jesus rose, Paul rose too as a new person, with Christ's life living inside of him.

a-new-creation-for-kids.q: What is the main message that ties the whole "Letters to the Churches" series together?
options: Follow enough rules and God will accept you
Life will be easy if you believe in Jesus
You are loved, forgiven, equipped, not alone, and made new in Christ
Only perfect people can be close to God
a-new-creation-for-kids.why: The entire series — from the gospel to the armor of God to joy to being a new creation — points to one truth: in Christ, you are loved, forgiven, equipped for anything, never alone, and completely made new. That's the message of the letters.

a-new-heaven-and-new-earth-for-kids.q: Who received the vision of the new heaven and new earth?
a-new-heaven-and-new-earth-for-kids.why: John — the beloved disciple of Jesus — was exiled on the island of Patmos when Jesus gave him the incredible vision recorded in the book of Revelation, including the new heaven and new earth.

a-new-heaven-and-new-earth-for-kids.q: What did the voice from the throne promise about tears, death, and pain?
options: They would be completely wiped away — no more death, mourning, crying, or pain
They would only happen to bad people
They would become easier to deal with
a-new-heaven-and-new-earth-for-kids.why: The promise is total and complete — God will wipe every tear from their eyes, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be completely gone. Not reduced. Gone. The old order of things will have passed away forever.

a-new-heaven-and-new-earth-for-kids.q: What did Jesus say from the throne about what He is doing?
options: "I am leaving all things as they are"
a-new-heaven-and-new-earth-for-kids.why: Jesus said "I am making everything new" — not just fixing or repairing the old world, but creating something entirely new and perfect. This is the ultimate promise: everything broken will be made brand new.

abraham-and-isaac-for-kids.q: What does the name "Isaac" mean, and why was he given that name?
options: "Strong one" — because he was a powerful baby
"Laughter" — because Sarah laughed when God said she'd have a baby at 90
"Gift" — because he was a gift from God
abraham-and-isaac-for-kids.why: Sarah laughed when God told her she'd have a son at ninety years old — it seemed impossible! So when the baby came, they named him Isaac, meaning "laughter."

abraham-and-isaac-for-kids.q: When Isaac asked where the lamb for the sacrifice was, what did Abraham say?
options: "There is no lamb — you are the sacrifice"
"God Himself will provide the lamb, my son"
abraham-and-isaac-for-kids.why: Abraham's answer showed incredible faith — even in the most difficult moment of his life, he trusted that God would make a way. And God did.

abraham-and-isaac-for-kids.q: What did God provide as a substitute sacrifice instead of Isaac?
options: A ram caught in a bush by its horns
abraham-and-isaac-for-kids.why: At the very last moment, Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. God provided the sacrifice, just as Abraham had believed He would.

absaloms-rebellion-for-kids.q: How did Absalom steal the hearts of the people?
options: He stood at the city gate and promised them better justice

absaloms-rebellion-for-kids.q: Where did Absalom declare himself king?
How did David leave Jerusalem when Absalom took over?
options: On a chariot in full armor

an-angel-visits-mary-for-kids.q: What was the name of the angel God sent to Mary?
an-angel-visits-mary-for-kids.why: God sent the angel Gabriel to deliver the most important birth announcement in history — that Mary would be the mother of Jesus, the Son of the Most High.

an-angel-visits-mary-for-kids.q: What was Mary's response when the angel told her God's plan?
options: "I am the Lord's servant. Let it be."
an-angel-visits-mary-for-kids.why: Even though she was young and knew it wouldn't be easy, Mary trusted God and said yes — "I am the Lord's servant. Let it be."

an-angel-visits-mary-for-kids.q: What happened when Mary visited her cousin Elizabeth?
options: The baby inside Elizabeth leaped and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit
Elizabeth was angry that Mary came without warning
an-angel-visits-mary-for-kids.why: The moment Elizabeth heard Mary's voice, the baby inside her (John the Baptist) leaped for joy, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit — confirming that Mary was carrying the Son of God.

ananias-and-sapphira-for-kids.q: What did Ananias and Sapphira sell?
What was the actual problem with what Ananias and Sapphira did?
options: They kept some money for themselves
They lied about how much they received and pretended to give everything
They gave too much money away

ananias-and-sapphira-for-kids.q: According to Peter, who did Ananias really lie to?

balaams-donkey-for-kids.q: Why did King Balak hire the prophet Balaam?
options: To lead his army into battle
balaams-donkey-for-kids.why: King Balak of Moab was terrified of the Israelites because he saw how powerful they were with God on their side. He hired the prophet Balaam to place a curse on Israel, believing that would weaken them. But you can't curse what God has blessed!

balaams-donkey-for-kids.q: Why did Balaam's donkey keep stopping and swerving off the road?
options: She could see the angel of the Lord blocking the path
She was scared of the Moabite army
balaams-donkey-for-kids.why: An angel of the Lord stood in the road with a drawn sword to stop Balaam. The donkey could see the angel even though Balaam couldn't. Each time the donkey tried to avoid the angel, Balaam beat her — not realizing the donkey was actually saving his life.

balaams-donkey-for-kids.q: What happened every time Balaam tried to curse Israel?
options: Blessings came out of his mouth instead of curses
balaams-donkey-for-kids.why: Three separate times, King Balak set up altars and asked Balaam to curse Israel. But every single time Balaam opened his mouth, God put blessings there instead. No one can override what God has declared — if He says you are blessed, you are blessed, period.

barnabas-the-encourager-for-kids.why: Barnabas's real name was Joseph, but the apostles nicknamed him "Barnabas," which means "Son of Encouragement." He was so consistently uplifting and supportive that encouragement literally became his identity.

barnabas-the-encourager-for-kids.q: What did Barnabas do when the other believers were afraid of the newly converted Saul?
options: He told Saul to leave Jerusalem and never come back
He hid from Saul just like everyone else
He vouched for Saul and brought him to the apostles
He wrote a letter to Saul asking him to prove himself first
barnabas-the-encourager-for-kids.why: When every believer in Jerusalem was terrified of Saul and refused to go near him, Barnabas stepped up. He took Saul to the apostles, told them about his conversion, and convinced them he was genuine. Without this one act of courage and encouragement, Paul might never have been accepted into the church.

barnabas-the-encourager-for-kids.q: What did Barnabas do when he was sent to the growing church in Antioch?
options: He shut the church down because Gentiles were involved
He encouraged the new believers and then brought Saul to help teach them
He reported back to Jerusalem that the church was failing
He left immediately because he didn't agree with what was happening
barnabas-the-encourager-for-kids.why: Barnabas saw what God was doing in Antioch and encouraged the believers to remain faithful. Then he traveled to find Saul and brought him back to help teach and mentor the church for an entire year. Barnabas always saw potential in people and pulled them into the mission.

behold-i-am-coming-soon-for-kids.q: When Jesus says "I am the Alpha and the Omega," what does that mean?
options: He is the First and the Last — He existed before everything and will exist after everything
He was the first person to be born and the last to die
Alpha and Omega are the names of two angels
behold-i-am-coming-soon-for-kids.why: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet and Omega is the last. By calling Himself the Alpha and the Omega, Jesus is saying He is the Beginning and the End — He was there before anything existed and He will be there when all things are made new.

behold-i-am-coming-soon-for-kids.q: What is the very last prayer in the Bible?
behold-i-am-coming-soon-for-kids.why: The last prayer recorded in Scripture is "Come, Lord Jesus" — a simple, powerful cry from the heart asking Jesus to return. And Jesus answers it with "Yes, I am coming soon."

behold-i-am-coming-soon-for-kids.q: What is the one message that runs through the entire Bible — from Genesis to Revelation?
options: Follow the rules and you'll be okay
Good people win and bad people lose
God loves you, He has always loved you, and He is coming for you
Life is hard but try your best
behold-i-am-coming-soon-for-kids.why: From the very first verse of Genesis to the very last verse of Revelation, the Bible tells one story: God created you, loves you, came to rescue you, and is coming back for you. It's a love story — and you're the one He's coming for.

born-in-a-manger-for-kids.q: Why was there no room for Mary and Joseph in Bethlehem?
options: They arrived too late at night
The town was packed because of the census
A storm had destroyed all the buildings
born-in-a-manger-for-kids.why: Caesar Augustus had ordered a census, and everyone had to return to their ancestral hometown. Bethlehem was overflowing with people, and every inn and guest room was completely full.

options: A type of ancient crib made of gold
A small room in an inn
A feeding trough where animals eat
A blanket used for swaddling babies
born-in-a-manger-for-kids.why: A manger is a feeding trough — a box or container that animals eat out of. It was meant for hay and animal food, but it became the very first bed for the King of the universe.

born-in-a-manger-for-kids.q: Why did Jesus say He chose to be born in a manger instead of a palace?
options: Because His parents preferred the outdoors
Because He didn't come for the powerful — He came for everyone
Because God made a mistake with the timing
born-in-a-manger-for-kids.why: Jesus chose the most humble beginning possible to show that He came for all people — especially the overlooked and the struggling. His birth in a manger showed that God's kingdom is built on humility, not worldly power.

breakfast-on-the-beach-for-kids.q: How many fish did the disciples catch before Jesus told them where to cast their net?
options: None — they caught nothing all night
breakfast-on-the-beach-for-kids.why: They fished all night long and caught absolutely nothing. Every cast came up empty.

breakfast-on-the-beach-for-kids.q: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do from the shore?
options: Throw their net on the right side of the boat
Wait for Him to swim out to them
breakfast-on-the-beach-for-kids.why: Jesus called out, "Throw your net on the right side of the boat and you will find some." And did they ever.

breakfast-on-the-beach-for-kids.q: How many fish did they catch after following Jesus' instructions?
breakfast-on-the-beach-for-kids.why: One hundred and fifty-three large fish! So many they could not haul the net in, yet it did not break.

building-the-temple-for-kids.q: Who originally dreamed of building a temple for God?
building-the-temple-for-kids.why: King David had the dream, the passion, and even the blueprints to build God's temple. But God told David he wouldn't be the one to build it — that honor would go to his son Solomon. The dream passed from father to son.

building-the-temple-for-kids.q: How many years did it take to build Solomon's temple?
building-the-temple-for-kids.why: The temple took seven years of meticulous construction to complete. Seven years of precision craftsmanship, artistic detail, and total dedication to creating the most magnificent building the world had ever seen.

building-the-temple-for-kids.q: What was unique about the construction at the actual building site?
options: It was built entirely at night
No hammer, chisel, or iron tool was heard — all stones were cut offsite
Only priests were allowed to work there
It was built in complete darkness
building-the-temple-for-kids.why: Every stone was precisely cut and shaped at the quarry, miles away from Jerusalem, then transported to the building site ready to be placed. The temple rose in near silence — there was something sacred about how God's house was built.

cain-and-abel-for-kids.q: Why was God pleased with Abel's offering but not Cain's?
options: God liked animals more than plants
Abel gave his very best while Cain didn't
Cain forgot to bring his offering on time
cain-and-abel-for-kids.why: It wasn't about what they brought — it was about the heart behind the gift. Abel gave God his absolute best, while Cain gave whatever was convenient.

cain-and-abel-for-kids.q: What did God warn Cain that sin was doing?
options: It was running away from him
It was crouching at his door like a wild animal ready to attack
It was hiding in the field
cain-and-abel-for-kids.why: God gave Cain a vivid and powerful warning — sin was like a predator crouching at his door, ready to pounce. But Cain had the power to master it.

cain-and-abel-for-kids.q: Even after what Cain did, how did God show mercy?
options: He let Cain go back to the garden
He put a protective mark on Cain so no one would kill him
cain-and-abel-for-kids.why: Even after Cain committed the worst possible act, God still showed mercy by protecting him with a special mark — showing how deep God's mercy goes.

calming-the-storm-for-kids.q: Where were Jesus and his disciples going when the storm hit?
calming-the-storm-for-kids.why: Jesus told His disciples, "Let's cross to the other side of the lake" — the Sea of Galilee.

calming-the-storm-for-kids.q: What was Jesus doing when the storm started?
calming-the-storm-for-kids.why: Jesus was so exhausted from a long day of teaching that He fell asleep on a cushion in the back of the boat.

calming-the-storm-for-kids.q: What did the disciples shout when they woke Jesus up?
calming-the-storm-for-kids.why: The disciples were so scared and frustrated that they asked Jesus, "Don't you care if we drown?!"

chariots-of-fire-for-kids.q: Why was the king of Syria frustrated with his battle plans?
options: Elisha kept warning the king of Israel about every ambush
The weather kept ruining his strategy
chariots-of-fire-for-kids.why: Every time the Syrian king set up a secret ambush, Elisha told the Israelite king exactly where it was. The Syrian king thought he had a spy — but it was actually a prophet hearing from God.

chariots-of-fire-for-kids.q: How did Elisha know the Syrian king's secret plans?
options: He had spies in the Syrian army
God revealed them to him — even words spoken in private rooms
chariots-of-fire-for-kids.why: God told Elisha everything — even the words the Syrian king spoke in his own bedroom. Nothing is hidden from God, and He shared what Elisha needed to know to protect Israel.

chariots-of-fire-for-kids.q: What did the Syrian king send to capture Elisha?
options: Horses, chariots, and a massive army that surrounded the entire city
chariots-of-fire-for-kids.why: The king didn't take any chances. He sent a huge force — horses, chariots, and a strong army — to surround the city of Dothan in the middle of the night. All of that to capture ONE prophet. That tells you how much they feared Elisha.

choosing-to-serve-for-kids.q: What did Joshua do before giving the people his famous challenge?
options: He showed them a map of the Promised Land
He recounted everything God had done — from Abraham to Egypt to the wilderness to the Promised Land
He listed all the battles they still needed to fight
He introduced the next leader of Israel
choosing-to-serve-for-kids.why: Before his big challenge, Joshua reminded the people of their entire history with God. He walked them through Abraham's calling, slavery in Egypt, the Exodus, the wilderness wandering, crossing the Jordan, and the conquest of the land. He wanted them to SEE God's faithfulness before he asked them to choose.

choosing-to-serve-for-kids.q: What is the famous line Joshua told the people of Israel?
options: "Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding"
"The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want"
"Choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord"
"Be strong and courageous, for the Lord your God is with you"
choosing-to-serve-for-kids.why: This is one of the most quoted verses in the entire Bible! Joshua made it clear that faith requires a personal choice. He couldn't make the decision for the people — each person had to decide for themselves. And Joshua led by example, declaring that no matter what anyone else chose, HE and his family would serve God.

choosing-to-serve-for-kids.q: What is the key lesson about faith from this episode?
options: Faith is something you only need to think about on Sundays
Faith is a daily choice — every day you decide who you'll follow
Faith means never having any doubts
Faith only matters when you're in trouble
choosing-to-serve-for-kids.why: Joshua's challenge was about "this day" — today! Faith isn't a one-and-done decision you make once and forget about. It's a daily, ongoing choice. Every morning when you wake up, you have the opportunity to choose who you'll listen to, who you'll trust, and who you'll follow. That's what makes faith real and alive — it's chosen again and again.

cleansing-the-temple-for-kids.q: What did Jesus find happening inside the temple?
options: Merchants overcharging for animals and money changers cheating people
The disciples setting up chairs for a sermon
cleansing-the-temple-for-kids.why: Merchants were selling sacrificial animals at inflated prices and money changers were cheating people. God's house of prayer had been turned into a den of robbers.

cleansing-the-temple-for-kids.q: What did Jesus make out of cords?
options: A rope to tie the doors shut
A whip to drive out the merchants
cleansing-the-temple-for-kids.why: A whip. Jesus made a whip out of cords and used it to drive the merchants and money changers out of the temple.

cleansing-the-temple-for-kids.q: What did Jesus call the temple?
options: Both A and B — it was supposed to be a house of prayer, but they had made it a den of robbers
cleansing-the-temple-for-kids.why: Jesus said "My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers." He quoted the prophet Isaiah and the prophet Jeremiah together.

crossing-the-red-sea-for-kids.q: What did Pharaoh do after he let the Israelites go?
options: He changed his mind and chased them with his army
He sent them gifts for the journey
crossing-the-red-sea-for-kids.why: Pharaoh regretted letting the Israelites leave and sent his entire army with chariots and horses to chase them down and bring them back.

crossing-the-red-sea-for-kids.q: What did God use to part the Red Sea?
options: Moses clapping his hands three times
A powerful east wind that blew all night after Moses stretched out his staff
A bolt of lightning that struck the water
crossing-the-red-sea-for-kids.why: God told Moses to stretch his staff over the sea, and then God sent a powerful east wind that blew all night long, splitting the waters and creating dry ground in the middle.

crossing-the-red-sea-for-kids.q: What did the Israelites do after they crossed the Red Sea safely?
options: They turned around and went back to Egypt
They sang a victory song praising God
They set up camp and went to sleep
crossing-the-red-sea-for-kids.why: After witnessing God's incredible rescue, the Israelites celebrated with singing and dancing. Miriam grabbed a tambourine, and they sang a song praising God as their strength and salvation.

cyrus-sets-them-free-for-kids.q: How many years were the Jewish people in Babylon before they were allowed to go home?
cyrus-sets-them-free-for-kids.why: The Jewish people were in Babylon for 70 years, just as God had promised through the prophet Jeremiah.

cyrus-sets-them-free-for-kids.q: Who was the king that let the Jewish people return to Jerusalem?
cyrus-sets-them-free-for-kids.why: Cyrus, king of Persia, issued the decree that allowed God's people to go home and rebuild the temple.

cyrus-sets-them-free-for-kids.q: How many years BEFORE Cyrus was born did the prophet Isaiah write down his name?
cyrus-sets-them-free-for-kids.why: Isaiah named Cyrus about 150 years before he was even born, showing that God knows the future completely.

dancing-before-the-lord-for-kids.q: Why did David want to bring the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem?
options: To show off his power as king
He wanted God's presence at the center of his city
The Ark was made of gold and very valuable
His army needed it for battle

dancing-before-the-lord-for-kids.q: What went wrong the first time David tried to move the Ark?
options: The cart broke apart on the road
Uzzah touched the Ark and died because they were not carrying it God's way
The oxen ran away with the Ark

dancing-before-the-lord-for-kids.q: Where did David leave the Ark for three months?

daniel-in-the-lions-den-for-kids.q: Why were the other officials jealous of Daniel?
options: Daniel was younger than all of them
Daniel had more money than the king
King Darius planned to put Daniel in charge of the entire kingdom
daniel-in-the-lions-den-for-kids.why: Daniel was so trustworthy and excellent at his job that King Darius planned to set him over the whole kingdom — and the other officials couldn't stand it.

daniel-in-the-lions-den-for-kids.q: What did Daniel do when he heard about the new law banning prayer?
options: He hid in a closet to pray secretly
He stopped praying for thirty days
He opened his windows and prayed three times a day, same as always
daniel-in-the-lions-den-for-kids.why: Daniel didn't hide, compromise, or run. He went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, and prayed on his knees three times a day — exactly as he always had.

daniel-in-the-lions-den-for-kids.q: How did God protect Daniel in the lions' den?
options: He sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths
He put the lions to sleep with thunder
daniel-in-the-lions-den-for-kids.why: Daniel told King Darius, "My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths." Daniel wasn't hurt at all — not a single scratch.

daniels-resolve-for-kids.q: Why did King Nebuchadnezzar select the best young men from the Jewish captives?
options: To send them back to Judah as leaders
To train them to serve in his royal court
To put them to work building temples
To use them as soldiers in his army
daniels-resolve-for-kids.why: Nebuchadnezzar wanted to absorb the brightest young men from conquered nations and train them to serve in the Babylonian court.

daniels-resolve-for-kids.q: Why did Daniel refuse to eat the king's food?
options: He was allergic to the food
The food violated God's laws and had been offered to idols
He was on a special diet
daniels-resolve-for-kids.why: The royal food had been offered to Babylonian idols and violated God's dietary laws. Daniel chose to honor God over comfort.

daniels-resolve-for-kids.q: What did Daniel ask to eat and drink instead?
daniels-resolve-for-kids.why: Daniel respectfully requested vegetables and water as an alternative to the king's rich food.

david-and-goliath-for-kids.q: How long did Goliath challenge the army of Israel before David arrived?
Why did David originally come to the battlefield?
options: His father sent him to deliver food to his brothers

david-and-goliath-for-kids.q: What had David already fought and killed before facing Goliath?
options: An eagle and a wild boar
A Philistine soldier and a bandit

david-and-jonathan-for-kids.q: What happened between Jonathan and David after the Goliath victory?
options: Jonathan challenged David to a fight
Jonathan's soul was knit to David's and they became best friends

david-and-jonathan-for-kids.q: What did Jonathan give to David as a sign of their bond?
options: His robe, armor, sword, and bow

david-and-jonathan-for-kids.q: Why did Saul become jealous of David?
options: David was taller and stronger than Saul
The women sang that David had killed ten thousands while Saul only thousands
David refused to play music for Saul

david-and-mephibosheth-for-kids.q: Why did David want to show kindness to someone from Saul's family?
options: He felt guilty about defeating Saul in battle
He made a promise to Jonathan and wanted to honor their friendship
His advisors told him it would make him popular
He needed more servants in the palace

david-and-mephibosheth-for-kids.q: What was Mephibosheth's relationship to Jonathan?

options: He was injured in a battle
His nurse dropped him while fleeing after Saul and Jonathan died
He fell from a horse as a teenager

david-becomes-king-for-kids.q: Which tribe anointed David as king first?
What city did David conquer and make his capital?
What did David bring to Jerusalem to put God at the center of his kingdom?

david-on-the-run-for-kids.q: How many soldiers did Saul send to hunt David?
What kind of people gathered around David at the cave of Adullam?
options: People in distress, in debt, and discontented
Priests and prophets from the temple

david-on-the-run-for-kids.q: About how many men joined David's group?

david-spares-his-enemy-for-kids.q: Where was David hiding when Saul unknowingly walked in?
options: A house in a nearby village

david-spares-his-enemy-for-kids.q: What did David do instead of killing Saul in the cave?
options: He snuck out the back entrance
He threw a rock at Saul
He cut off a corner of Saul's robe
He captured Saul and tied him up

david-spares-his-enemy-for-kids.q: What did David say about why he wouldn't harm Saul?
options: "Saul is too powerful for me to fight"
"I will not touch the LORD's anointed"
"I'm saving him for a public trial"

davids-big-mistake-for-kids.q: What was David's first mistake in this story?
options: He lost a battle against the Philistines
He stayed home from battle when he should have been leading his army
He forgot to pray in the morning
He argued with Nathan the prophet

davids-big-mistake-for-kids.q: Instead of confessing his sin, what did David try to do?
options: He tried to cover it up, and it only got worse
He asked God to make everyone forget

davids-big-mistake-for-kids.q: Why was Uriah such an honorable man?
options: He refused to enjoy comfort at home while his fellow soldiers were fighting
He volunteered for extra battle duty
He gave all his money to the poor
He built a temple for God

davids-final-words-for-kids.q: What was David's greatest dream that he could not fulfill himself?
options: Building a permanent temple for God

davids-final-words-for-kids.q: Why did God say David couldn't build the temple?
options: David had been a man of war
David didn't have the right skills

davids-final-words-for-kids.q: What did David give from his personal fortune for the temple?
options: Thousands of talents of his own gold and silver

davids-repentance-for-kids.q: Who did God send to confront David about his sin?
When David was confronted, how did he respond?
options: He made excuses and blamed others
He owned his sin completely and asked God for mercy
He ran away from the prophet

davids-repentance-for-kids.q: What famous line did David write in Psalm 51?
options: "Create in me a clean heart, O God"
"Be still and know that I am God"

deborah-a-brave-leader-for-kids.q: What two roles did Deborah hold in Israel?
deborah-a-brave-leader-for-kids.why: Deborah was both a prophet — hearing directly from God — and a judge, meaning she was the leader of Israel. People came from across the nation to seek her guidance and wisdom under the palm tree where she held court.

deborah-a-brave-leader-for-kids.q: What condition did Barak give before agreeing to go into battle?
options: He would only go if Deborah came with him
He wanted to wait until the next year
deborah-a-brave-leader-for-kids.why: When Deborah told Barak that God commanded him to lead the army against Sisera, Barak said he would only go if Deborah went with him. She agreed, but told him the glory for defeating Sisera would go to a woman instead of to him.

deborah-a-brave-leader-for-kids.q: How was the enemy commander Sisera ultimately defeated?
options: He fell off a cliff while running away
Jael defeated him with a tent peg while he slept
A flood swept away his chariots
deborah-a-brave-leader-for-kids.why: After fleeing the lost battle on foot, Sisera hid in Jael's tent, thinking he was safe. Jael gave him shelter and a drink, but when he fell asleep, she used a tent peg to end the threat of Sisera permanently — fulfilling Deborah's prophecy that the glory would go to a woman.

do-not-worry-for-kids.q: What did Jesus point to as an example of God's care and provision?
options: The birds of the air and the wildflowers
The fish in the sea and the trees in the forest
do-not-worry-for-kids.why: Jesus pointed to the birds — who don't plant or harvest yet God feeds them — and the wildflowers, which are dressed more beautifully than King Solomon, to show that God takes care of His creation and will take care of you even more.

do-not-worry-for-kids.q: What does Jesus say worrying can add to your life?
options: A single hour — but that's it
Nothing at all — not a single hour
do-not-worry-for-kids.why: Jesus asked, "Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to your life?" The answer is no one. Worry doesn't fix anything or add anything — it only steals your peace.

do-not-worry-for-kids.q: According to Philippians 4:6-7, what happens when you bring your worries to God in prayer?
options: God immediately removes all your problems
You feel worse before you feel better
The peace of God, which transcends all understanding, guards your heart and mind
God gives you a list of things to do to fix it yourself
do-not-worry-for-kids.why: Paul promised that when we bring our worries to God through prayer with thanksgiving, God gives us a peace so deep it goes beyond what we can even understand — and that peace guards our hearts and minds like a shield.

doubting-thomas-for-kids.q: Why was Thomas not with the other disciples when Jesus first appeared?
options: He was in a different city
He had stepped out and missed it
He was too afraid to come
He had given up being a disciple
doubting-thomas-for-kids.why: Thomas simply was not there when Jesus appeared to the group. He missed the moment, which set up his struggle with doubt.

doubting-thomas-for-kids.q: What did Thomas say he would need in order to believe Jesus was alive?
options: He wanted to hear Jesus preach again
He wanted the other disciples to prove it with evidence
He wanted to see the nail marks in Jesus' hands and put his finger in them, and put his hand in Jesus' side
He wanted an angel to tell him
doubting-thomas-for-kids.why: Thomas set a very specific and physical standard for belief. He wanted to see and touch the wounds himself.

doubting-thomas-for-kids.q: How long did Thomas wait before Jesus appeared again?
doubting-thomas-for-kids.why: Thomas sat with his doubt for seven full days while everyone around him was celebrating. Then, the following Sunday, Jesus came again.

elijah-and-the-ravens-for-kids.q: Who was the wicked king ruling Israel when Elijah appeared?
What bold announcement did Elijah make to the king?
options: "There will be no rain until I say so"

elijah-and-the-ravens-for-kids.q: Where did God tell Elijah to hide after confronting the king?
options: In a cave on Mount Sinai

elijah-taken-to-heaven-for-kids.q: What did Elisha keep saying when Elijah told him to stay behind?
options: "As surely as the Lord lives, I will not leave you"
"Let me say goodbye to my family first"
elijah-taken-to-heaven-for-kids.why: Every time Elijah told Elisha to stay, Elisha gave the same passionate response — he refused to leave Elijah's side. His loyalty and hunger for God's presence kept him right where he needed to be.

elijah-taken-to-heaven-for-kids.q: What did Elijah use to part the Jordan River?
elijah-taken-to-heaven-for-kids.why: Elijah rolled up his cloak and struck the water with it. The Jordan parted, and they walked across on dry ground — an incredible display of God's power working through an ordinary piece of clothing.

elijah-taken-to-heaven-for-kids.q: What did Elisha ask Elijah for before he was taken away?
options: The location of a hidden treasure
A double portion of his spirit
elijah-taken-to-heaven-for-kids.why: Elisha made one of the boldest requests in the Bible — a double portion of Elijah's spirit. He wasn't asking for twice the power to show off; he was asking for the spiritual inheritance to carry God's work forward.

elisha-double-portion-for-kids.q: What happened when Elisha struck the Jordan River with Elijah's cloak?
options: The water parted and he walked across on dry ground
elisha-double-portion-for-kids.why: Elisha struck the water and it split right down the middle, just as it had for Elijah. This was the first proof that God's power — the double portion — now rested on Elisha.

elisha-double-portion-for-kids.q: What did the watching prophets declare after seeing the Jordan part?
options: "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha"
"We should follow Elisha to the ends of the earth"
elisha-double-portion-for-kids.why: The prophets recognized immediately that the same spirit and power that had been on Elijah had now transferred to Elisha. A new era of prophetic ministry was beginning.

elisha-double-portion-for-kids.q: What was wrong with the water in Jericho?
options: It was too salty to drink
It was bad and making the land unproductive
elisha-double-portion-for-kids.why: The people of Jericho told Elisha that while the city's location was good, the water was bad — it was poisoning the land and nothing would grow. Contaminated water meant contaminated life.

escape-to-egypt-for-kids.q: How did Joseph know to flee to Egypt with his family?
options: The wise men warned him before they left
An angel appeared to him in a dream
Mary had a vision during the night
escape-to-egypt-for-kids.why: God sent an angel to Joseph in a dream with an urgent message — take the child and His mother and flee to Egypt immediately because Herod wanted to kill Jesus.

escape-to-egypt-for-kids.q: Why was Herod so angry at the wise men?
options: They didn't bring him any gifts
They never came back to tell him where Jesus was
They told everyone Herod was a bad king
They refused to enter his palace
escape-to-egypt-for-kids.why: Herod had asked the wise men to report back with the child's exact location so he could destroy Him. When they went home a different way — warned by God in a dream — Herod was furious that his plan had been ruined.

escape-to-egypt-for-kids.q: Where did Joseph's family settle after returning from Egypt?
escape-to-egypt-for-kids.why: After Herod died and the angel told Joseph it was safe to return, the family settled in the small town of Nazareth, where Jesus grew up.

esther-becomes-queen-for-kids.q: Why was Queen Vashti removed as queen?
options: She refused to come when the king summoned her
esther-becomes-queen-for-kids.why: Queen Vashti refused to appear before King Xerxes at his banquet, and the king removed her from her position as queen.

esther-becomes-queen-for-kids.q: How long did King Xerxes' original banquet celebration last?
esther-becomes-queen-for-kids.why: The king's display of wealth and power lasted an astonishing 180 days — that's six months of showing off his kingdom's glory.

esther-becomes-queen-for-kids.q: Who raised Esther after her parents died?
esther-becomes-queen-for-kids.why: Mordecai, Esther's older cousin, raised her as his own daughter after both her parents died. He loved her and guided her.

esther-saves-her-people-for-kids.q: What happened to King Xerxes the night before Esther's banquet?
options: He couldn't sleep and had the royal records read to him
esther-saves-her-people-for-kids.why: The king couldn't sleep, so he had the royal chronicles read aloud. In those records, he discovered that Mordecai had once saved his life by uncovering an assassination plot — and was never rewarded.

esther-saves-her-people-for-kids.q: What did Haman think when the king asked, "What should be done for a man the king wants to honor?"
options: He thought the king wanted to honor Mordecai
He thought the king was testing him
He thought the king was talking about himself (Haman)
He thought the king was joking
esther-saves-her-people-for-kids.why: Haman's ego was so enormous that he was convinced the king must be talking about honoring him. So he described the most extravagant honor he could imagine — and it all went to Mordecai instead.

esther-saves-her-people-for-kids.q: What did Esther reveal at her banquet?
options: That she was Jewish and that Haman was plotting to destroy her people
That she wanted to leave the palace
esther-saves-her-people-for-kids.why: Esther courageously revealed her Jewish identity and exposed Haman's genocidal plot right there at the dinner table, with the king and Haman both present.

ezra-reads-the-law-for-kids.q: How long did Ezra read the Law to the people?
options: From sunrise to midday — about 6 hours
ezra-reads-the-law-for-kids.why: Ezra read from sunrise to midday, which was roughly six hours. And the people stood and listened the entire time!

ezra-reads-the-law-for-kids.q: Who helped explain the meaning of the Law to the people as Ezra read?
ezra-reads-the-law-for-kids.why: The Levites walked among the crowd and helped the people understand the meaning of what was being read.

ezra-reads-the-law-for-kids.q: How did the people react when they heard and understood God's Law?
ezra-reads-the-law-for-kids.why: The people wept when they realized how far they had strayed from God's commands. The Word pierced their hearts.

faith-hall-of-fame-for-kids.q: What made Abel's offering special compared to Cain's?
options: It was his best — not his leftovers
faith-hall-of-fame-for-kids.why: Abel offered God his very best, and that's what made his sacrifice better.

faith-hall-of-fame-for-kids.q: What happened to Enoch because he walked so closely with God?
options: God took him — he never died
faith-hall-of-fame-for-kids.why: Enoch's faith was so real that God simply took him. He never experienced death.

faith-hall-of-fame-for-kids.q: Why did people laugh at Noah?
options: He was building a boat with no flood in sight
He was too old to build
He used the wrong kind of wood
faith-hall-of-fame-for-kids.why: There was no rain, no flood, no reason to build a boat — except that God said so. And that was enough for Noah.

faith-hope-and-love-for-kids.q: According to 1 Corinthians 13:13, which three things remain forever?
faith-hope-and-love-for-kids.why: "And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love." (1 Corinthians 13:13)

options: The substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen
Believing only what you can prove
faith-hope-and-love-for-kids.why: "Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen." (Hebrews 11:1)

faith-hope-and-love-for-kids.q: How is biblical hope DIFFERENT from ordinary wishing?
options: It's not — they're the same thing
Biblical hope is confident expectation based on God's promises
Biblical hope is just for adults
faith-hope-and-love-for-kids.why: Biblical hope isn't wishful thinking. It's confident expectation because it's based on the promises of a God who never lies and never fails.

faith-without-works-for-kids.q: In James's example, what does the person say to the hungry, cold brother or sister?
options: "Go in peace! Stay warm and well fed!" — but does nothing
faith-without-works-for-kids.why: James used this example to show how empty words are without action. Saying kind things while doing nothing is meaningless.

faith-without-works-for-kids.q: According to James, what is faith without works?
faith-without-works-for-kids.why: James didn't sugarcoat it. He said faith without works is dead — not struggling, not growing — dead. Like a body without a spirit.

faith-without-works-for-kids.q: Does James teach that good works EARN salvation?
options: Yes — you have to earn it
No — salvation is a gift, but real faith naturally produces action
faith-without-works-for-kids.why: Salvation is always a gift from God. But genuine faith changes you from the inside out, and that change shows in how you live.

feeding-the-five-thousand-for-kids.q: Which disciple did Jesus ask about buying bread for the crowd?
feeding-the-five-thousand-for-kids.why: Jesus asked Philip where they could buy bread, testing him — because Jesus already knew what He was going to do.

feeding-the-five-thousand-for-kids.q: How much did Philip say it would cost to feed the crowd?
feeding-the-five-thousand-for-kids.why: Philip calculated that more than eight months' wages wouldn't be enough to give everyone even a small bite.

feeding-the-five-thousand-for-kids.q: What food did the boy have?
options: Five barley loaves and two fish
feeding-the-five-thousand-for-kids.why: Andrew brought a boy who had five small barley loaves and two small fish — a simple, small lunch.

fire-from-heaven-for-kids.q: How many prophets of Baal gathered on Mount Carmel to face Elijah?
What was the challenge Elijah proposed?
options: A sword fight between the prophets
The god who answers by fire is the real God
A race to the top of the mountain
Whoever could make it rain first wins

fire-from-heaven-for-kids.q: What happened when the prophets of Baal called on their god?

gideon-the-unlikely-hero-for-kids.q: What was Gideon doing when the angel of the Lord appeared to him?
options: Threshing wheat in a winepress because he was hiding from the Midianites
gideon-the-unlikely-hero-for-kids.why: Gideon was so afraid of the Midianites that he was threshing wheat in a winepress — a hidden, low spot — instead of out in the open where it was normally done. He was trying to prepare food without being discovered by the enemy.

gideon-the-unlikely-hero-for-kids.q: What did the angel call Gideon when he first appeared?
gideon-the-unlikely-hero-for-kids.why: The angel greeted Gideon by saying "The Lord is with you, mighty warrior" — even though Gideon was hiding in fear at that very moment. God saw Gideon not as he was, but as who he would become.

gideon-the-unlikely-hero-for-kids.q: What did Gideon do with a fleece to test whether God was really calling him?
options: He used it as a flag to signal his army
He asked God to make it wet then dry on consecutive nights, and God did both
He sold it at the market for supplies
He wrapped it around his sword for battle
gideon-the-unlikely-hero-for-kids.why: Gideon placed a wool fleece on the ground and asked God to make it wet with dew while the ground stayed dry. When God did it, Gideon asked for the reverse — dry fleece, wet ground. God patiently did both, confirming His call on Gideon's life.

gideons-300-for-kids.q: Why did God tell Gideon he had too many soldiers?
options: Because a smaller army could move faster
Because God wanted everyone to know the victory came from Him, not from military strength
Because there wasn't enough food for all of them
Because most of them didn't have weapons
gideons-300-for-kids.why: God deliberately reduced Gideon's army from 32,000 to just 300 so that Israel could never boast that their own strength won the battle. The victory was so impossible by human standards that everyone would know God was the one who did it.

gideons-300-for-kids.q: How did God reduce the army from 10,000 to 300?
options: He picked only soldiers who had previous battle experience
He selected the men based on how they drank water at the river
He let the soldiers vote on who should stay
gideons-300-for-kids.why: God told Gideon to watch how the soldiers drank water. Most knelt down and put their faces in the water, but 300 men scooped water with their hands and lapped it while staying alert. God chose those 300 for the battle.

gideons-300-for-kids.q: What unusual "weapons" did Gideon's 300 soldiers use to defeat the Midianites?
options: Trumpets, clay jars, and torches hidden inside the jars
gideons-300-for-kids.why: Instead of traditional weapons, each of the 300 men carried a trumpet, a clay jar, and a torch hidden inside the jar. On Gideon's signal, they blew the trumpets, smashed the jars to reveal the torches, and shouted. The sudden noise and light caused the Midianites to panic and turn on each other.

god-calls-abraham-for-kids.q: What made God's command to Abram so challenging?
options: God asked him to fight a war
God told him to leave everything but didn't tell him where to go
God told him to build a tower
God asked him to give away all his money
god-calls-abraham-for-kids.why: God told Abram to leave his home, his people, and everything familiar — but didn't give him a destination. Abram had to trust God completely without knowing where he'd end up.

god-calls-abraham-for-kids.q: How old was Abram when he left Haran?
god-calls-abraham-for-kids.why: Abram was 75 years old when he set out — an age when most people would be settling down. Instead, he was starting the greatest adventure of his life.

god-calls-abraham-for-kids.q: What did God compare Abram's future descendants to?
options: The grains of sand on a beach
god-calls-abraham-for-kids.why: God took Abram outside at night and told him to try counting the stars — saying that's how many descendants he would have. An incredible promise for a man with no children.

god-calls-samuel-for-kids.q: How many times did God call Samuel's name before Samuel realized it was God?
options: Twice — Eli told him after the second time
Three times — Eli finally realized it was God calling
Five times — Samuel kept ignoring it
god-calls-samuel-for-kids.why: God called Samuel three times, and each time Samuel ran to Eli thinking the old priest had called him. After the third time, Eli realized that it was the Lord speaking to the boy and told Samuel how to respond.

god-calls-samuel-for-kids.q: What did Eli tell Samuel to say if God called again?
options: "Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening"
god-calls-samuel-for-kids.why: Eli instructed Samuel to respond with humility and openness: "Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening." This simple response showed willingness to hear and obey whatever God had to say.

god-calls-samuel-for-kids.q: What did Samuel grow up to become?
options: A king who ruled Israel for fifty years
A soldier who led Israel's armies
One of the greatest prophets in Israel's history
A farmer who supplied food to the temple
god-calls-samuel-for-kids.why: From that night when God first spoke to him, Samuel grew into one of Israel's most important prophets. He would anoint kings, guide the nation, and faithfully deliver God's words to the people for decades.

god-chooses-david-for-kids.q: Where did God send Samuel to find the next king?
options: To the battlefield against the Philistines

god-chooses-david-for-kids.q: When Samuel saw Jesse's oldest son Eliab, what did God tell him?
options: "This is the one — anoint him immediately"
"Don't look at his appearance — the Lord looks at the heart"

god-chooses-david-for-kids.q: How many of Jesse's sons passed before Samuel and were rejected by God?

gods-presence-for-kids.q: What did Moses ask God for after the golden calf incident?
options: A faster route to the promised land
A bigger army to protect the people
God's presence to go with them, and to see God's glory
Permission to go back to Egypt
gods-presence-for-kids.why: Moses told God that if His presence didn't go with them, he didn't want to go anywhere. Then Moses boldly asked to see God's glory, and God graciously allowed Moses to see His back as He passed by.

gods-presence-for-kids.q: What happened when the Tabernacle was finally completed and set up?
options: The people had a feast inside it
God's cloud of glory filled it so powerfully that even Moses couldn't enter
Lightning struck it and it caught fire
Nothing happened and the people were disappointed
gods-presence-for-kids.why: When the Tabernacle was finished, the cloud of God's glory came down and filled it so completely and powerfully that even Moses could not go inside. God had moved in to dwell right in the middle of His people's camp.

gods-presence-for-kids.q: What is the main point of the entire book of Exodus?
options: That Egypt was a bad place to live
That Moses was the greatest leader ever
That God rescues His people and then comes to live among them
That following rules is the most important thing
gods-presence-for-kids.why: The whole story of Exodus is about God rescuing His people from slavery and then choosing to live WITH them — first in the Tabernacle, and ultimately through Jesus (Emmanuel, meaning "God with us") and the Holy Spirit living in every believer.

gods-promise-to-david-for-kids.q: What did David want to build for God?
options: A temple — a permanent house for the Ark of God
A fortress to protect the city

gods-promise-to-david-for-kids.q: Who was the prophet that God spoke through to deliver His message to David?
What was God's surprising response to David's plan?
options: He told David to build the temple immediately
He said David's plan was too expensive
He said David would not build God a house — God would build David's house instead
He told David to ask Solomon first

good-kings-and-bad-kings-for-kids.q: What did Jeroboam set up in the Northern Kingdom that led Israel into idol worship?
options: A new temple made of silver
good-kings-and-bad-kings-for-kids.why: Jeroboam was afraid his people would return to Jerusalem to worship, so he built two golden calves — one in Dan and one in Bethel — and told the people these were their gods. It echoed the same sin Israel committed at Mount Sinai.

good-kings-and-bad-kings-for-kids.q: What did King Hezekiah do when the Assyrian army surrounded Jerusalem?
options: He surrendered immediately to save lives
He fled the city and hid in the mountains
He took the threatening letter into the temple and prayed to God
He sent his army to fight Assyria alone
good-kings-and-bad-kings-for-kids.why: Instead of panicking or surrendering, Hezekiah brought the threatening letter before God in the temple and prayed for deliverance. That night, God sent an angel who defeated the Assyrian army of 185,000 soldiers.

good-kings-and-bad-kings-for-kids.q: How old was Josiah when he became king, and what did he find that changed the nation?
options: He was 18, and he found a hidden treasure of gold
He was 8, and workers found the lost Book of the Law in the temple
He was 30, and he discovered an ancient map
He was 12, and he found Solomon's crown
good-kings-and-bad-kings-for-kids.why: Josiah became king at just eight years old. When he was about twenty-six, workers repairing the temple discovered the forgotten Book of the Law. When Josiah heard it read, he wept, tore down every idol in the land, and led the greatest spiritual revival Judah had ever seen.

hamans-evil-plot-for-kids.q: Why was Haman so furious with Mordecai?
options: Mordecai refused to bow to Haman
hamans-evil-plot-for-kids.why: Mordecai refused to bow down to Haman because he bowed to God alone. Haman's ego couldn't handle the fact that one man wouldn't kneel before him.

hamans-evil-plot-for-kids.q: What did Haman plot to do in response to Mordecai's defiance?
options: Destroy ALL the Jewish people in the entire empire
hamans-evil-plot-for-kids.why: Haman didn't just go after Mordecai. He plotted to wipe out every Jewish man, woman, and child across all 127 provinces of the Persian Empire.

hamans-evil-plot-for-kids.q: What would happen to anyone who approached the king without being invited?
options: They would be put to death unless the king extended his golden scepter
hamans-evil-plot-for-kids.why: Approaching the king uninvited was punishable by death. The only exception was if the king chose to extend his golden scepter, sparing that person's life.

hannahs-prayer-for-kids.q: Why was Hannah so deeply heartbroken?
options: She had lost her home in a flood
She couldn't have children, and Peninnah constantly mocked her for it
She was forced to leave her country
hannahs-prayer-for-kids.why: Hannah desperately wanted a child but couldn't have one. To make matters worse, Elkanah's other wife Peninnah had many children and constantly provoked Hannah about it, year after year.

hannahs-prayer-for-kids.q: What happened when the priest Eli saw Hannah praying at the temple?
options: He immediately blessed her and prayed with her
He thought she was drunk because her lips were moving but no sound came out
He told her to come back another day
hannahs-prayer-for-kids.why: Hannah was praying so intensely — from such a deep place of pain — that her lips moved but no words came out. Eli saw this and assumed she was drunk, but Hannah explained she was pouring her soul out to God.

hannahs-prayer-for-kids.q: What did Hannah do after God answered her prayer and gave her a son?
options: She kept Samuel at home and never went back to the temple
She asked God for more children instead
She kept her promise and brought Samuel to the temple to serve God for his whole life
She named him after the priest Eli
hannahs-prayer-for-kids.why: Hannah had vowed that if God gave her a son, she would give him back to God. After Samuel was born, she kept that incredible promise — bringing her miracle child to the temple to serve the Lord for his entire life. That's extraordinary faith.

healing-the-blind-man-for-kids.q: What did the disciples ask Jesus about the blind man?
options: "Who sinned — this man or his parents?"
healing-the-blind-man-for-kids.why: The disciples assumed someone's sin caused the blindness and asked, "Who sinned — this man or his parents?" Jesus corrected them.

healing-the-blind-man-for-kids.q: According to Jesus, why was the man born blind?
options: So that God's work could be displayed in his life
As a test for the disciples
healing-the-blind-man-for-kids.why: Jesus said, "Neither this man nor his parents sinned. This happened so that the works of God might be displayed in him."

healing-the-blind-man-for-kids.q: What did Jesus put on the blind man's eyes?
options: Mud made from spit and dirt
healing-the-blind-man-for-kids.why: Jesus spit on the ground, made mud, and put it on the man's eyes — then told him to go wash in the Pool of Siloam.

healing-the-sick-for-kids.q: Who was the first person Jesus healed in this episode?
What happened at sunset outside Peter's house?
options: The whole town brought their sick to Jesus

healing-the-sick-for-kids.q: Why were lepers forced to live alone?
options: They were considered unclean and nobody would come near them
They chose to live in the wilderness

i-am-the-way-for-kids.q: What did Jesus tell His disciples not to let happen?
options: "Do not let your hands be idle"
"Do not let your hearts be troubled"
"Do not let your faith be tested"
i-am-the-way-for-kids.why: Jesus saw how afraid and worried His disciples were, so He told them, "Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God — believe also in me." He wanted them to trust Him even when things looked scary.

i-am-the-way-for-kids.q: Which disciple asked, "How can we know the way?"
i-am-the-way-for-kids.why: Thomas was the one who spoke up honestly and said, "Lord, we don't even know where you're going. How can we know the way?" And Jesus gave him one of the most famous answers in the Bible.

i-am-the-way-for-kids.q: When Jesus said "I am the way, the truth, and the life," what was He teaching?
options: That there are many different paths to God
That following rules is the most important thing
That He Himself — not a religion or philosophy — is the path to God
That only certain people can know God
i-am-the-way-for-kids.why: Jesus didn't point to a system or a set of instructions. He said HE is the way to God. The path to the Father isn't a thing — it's a person. Knowing Jesus IS knowing God.

in-the-beginning-creation-for-kids.q: What were the very first words God spoke?
in-the-beginning-creation-for-kids.why: God spoke "Let there be light" and light burst into existence — that was the very first thing He created on Day One.

in-the-beginning-creation-for-kids.q: What did God use to form Adam?
in-the-beginning-creation-for-kids.why: God scooped up dust from the ground and formed Adam, then breathed life into him — making humans uniquely personal among all creation.

in-the-beginning-creation-for-kids.q: Why did God rest on the seventh day?
options: Creating the universe made Him tired
He ran out of things to create
To give us the gift of rest and show that rest matters
Because Adam asked Him to stop
in-the-beginning-creation-for-kids.why: God didn't rest because He was tired — He rested to set an example and show us that rest is an important gift.

isaiahs-promise-for-kids.why: Isaiah prophesied that a virgin would give birth to a son called Immanuel, which means "God with us" — a promise that God Himself would come to be among His people.

isaiahs-promise-for-kids.q: Which of these is NOT one of the names Isaiah gave to the promised child?
isaiahs-promise-for-kids.why: Isaiah 9 names the child Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace. "Conquering Warrior" is not one of the titles Isaiah used.

isaiahs-promise-for-kids.q: What does Isaiah 53 describe about the coming servant?
options: A powerful king who would conquer every nation by force
A suffering servant who would be pierced for our sins and heal us by his wounds
A wealthy ruler who would make Israel the richest nation
A priest who would rebuild Solomon's Temple
isaiahs-promise-for-kids.why: Isaiah 53 describes a servant who would be despised, rejected, pierced for our transgressions, and crushed for our sins — and that by his wounds, we would be healed. Jesus fulfilled every detail of this prophecy.

israel-wants-a-king-for-kids.q: Why did the people of Israel want a new leader instead of Samuel's sons?
options: Samuel's sons moved to another country
Samuel's sons were dishonest and took bribes
Samuel's sons were too young to lead
Samuel's sons wanted to be farmers instead

israel-wants-a-king-for-kids.q: What did the elders of Israel ask Samuel to give them?
options: A king like all the other nations

israel-wants-a-king-for-kids.q: What did God tell Samuel when the people demanded a king?
options: "They have rejected you as their leader"
"They have rejected ME as their king"
"They are wise to ask for a king"
"Tell them to wait ten more years"

it-is-finished-for-kids.q: What happened to the sky while Jesus was on the cross?
options: Darkness covered the land for three hours
Stars became visible in the daytime
it-is-finished-for-kids.why: Darkness covered the entire land from noon to three in the afternoon. The sun itself stopped shining during the most important hours in history.

it-is-finished-for-kids.q: What did Jesus cry out during the darkness?
options: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
it-is-finished-for-kids.why: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" For the first time in all of eternity, Jesus experienced separation from His Father as He bore the weight of the world's sin.

it-is-finished-for-kids.q: What does the word "Tetelestai" — the word Jesus used when He said "It is finished" — mean?
it-is-finished-for-kids.why: "Paid in full." Jesus wasn't saying He was defeated. He was declaring that the debt for sin was completely settled — nothing left to pay.

jacob-and-esau-for-kids.q: What did Esau trade his birthright for?
jacob-and-esau-for-kids.why: Esau was so hungry and focused on what he wanted in the moment that he gave up his birthright — his entire future inheritance and family leadership — for a single bowl of red stew.

jacob-and-esau-for-kids.q: What new name did God give Jacob after they wrestled, and what does it mean?
jacob-and-esau-for-kids.why: God changed Jacob's name from "deceiver" to Israel — "one who wrestles with God and overcomes." It marked a complete transformation of his identity. The entire nation of Israel is named after him.

jacob-and-esau-for-kids.q: How did Esau react when he finally saw Jacob again after twenty years?
options: He attacked him and demanded his birthright back
He refused to speak to him
He ran to him, hugged him, and wept
jacob-and-esau-for-kids.why: After twenty years of hurt and betrayal, Esau chose forgiveness. He ran to Jacob, embraced him, and wept — one of the most beautiful moments of reconciliation in the Bible.

jairus-daughter-for-kids.why: Jairus was an important synagogue leader who humbled himself, fell at Jesus' feet, and begged Him to come heal his dying daughter.

jairus-daughter-for-kids.q: What happened to the woman who touched Jesus' cloak?
options: She was healed after 12 years of bleeding
jairus-daughter-for-kids.why: The woman had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years and had spent all her money on doctors. The moment she touched Jesus' cloak in faith, she was instantly healed.

jairus-daughter-for-kids.q: What bad news did the messengers bring from Jairus's house?
jairus-daughter-for-kids.why: Messengers came and told Jairus, "Your daughter is dead. Don't bother the teacher anymore."

john-the-baptist-for-kids.q: What was John the Baptist's main message to the people?
options: "Follow me and I will make you rich"
"Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is near!"
"Come to the temple and offer sacrifices"
"Leave Israel and start over somewhere new"
john-the-baptist-for-kids.why: John's urgent message was "Repent!" — calling people to turn away from their sins and prepare their hearts because God's Kingdom was about to arrive through Jesus.

john-the-baptist-for-kids.q: What did John call the Pharisees and Sadducees when they came to see him?
john-the-baptist-for-kids.why: John boldly called the religious leaders a "brood of vipers" — a bunch of snakes — because they looked religious on the outside but hadn't truly changed their hearts.

john-the-baptist-for-kids.q: What did John say about the one coming after him?
options: "He will be a great teacher like me"
"He will build a new temple in Jerusalem"
"I'm not even worthy to untie His sandals — He will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire"
"He will be a mighty warrior who defeats Rome"
john-the-baptist-for-kids.why: John made it clear that Jesus was infinitely greater than him. While John baptized with water, Jesus would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire — something only God could do.

jonah-running-from-god-for-kids.q: Why did Jonah run away from God's command?
options: He didn't want to help Nineveh — Israel's enemies — get a chance to repent
He didn't believe God was real
He wanted to go on vacation
jonah-running-from-god-for-kids.why: Nineveh was the capital of Assyria, the empire that destroyed Northern Israel. Jonah didn't want God to show mercy to his people's worst enemies, so he ran in the opposite direction.

jonah-running-from-god-for-kids.q: What happened to Jonah after the sailors threw him overboard?
options: A huge fish swallowed him and he stayed inside for three days
He floated on a piece of wood
A dolphin carried him back to the ship
jonah-running-from-god-for-kids.why: God sent a huge fish that swallowed Jonah whole. He spent three days and three nights inside the fish before it vomited him onto dry land.

jonah-running-from-god-for-kids.q: What connection did Jesus make between Jonah's story and His own?
options: Just as Jonah spent three days in the fish, Jesus spent three days in the tomb
They both ran away from God
jonah-running-from-god-for-kids.why: Jesus pointed out that Jonah's three days in the belly of the fish foreshadowed His own three days in the tomb before His resurrection — Jonah's story was pointing to Jesus all along.

jonah-the-lesson-for-kids.q: What happened when Jonah preached to the people of Nineveh?
options: They laughed at him and ignored his message
They chased him out of the city
The entire city repented — from the king down to the animals in sackcloth
jonah-the-lesson-for-kids.why: In one of the most shocking responses in the Bible, the entire city of Nineveh repented. The king himself got off his throne, put on sackcloth, and commanded everyone — even the animals — to fast and cry out to God.

jonah-the-lesson-for-kids.q: Why was Jonah angry after Nineveh was spared?
options: He wanted to be paid for his preaching
He knew God was gracious and merciful, and he didn't want Nineveh's enemies to be forgiven
He was upset about the long walk
jonah-the-lesson-for-kids.why: Jonah admitted he ran in the first place because he knew God was compassionate and would forgive Nineveh. He didn't want Israel's worst enemies to receive God's mercy.

jonah-the-lesson-for-kids.q: What lesson did God teach Jonah through the vine?
options: That plants are more important than people
That Jonah should become a gardener
That Jonah cared more about his own comfort than about 120,000 people
That the sun is too hot in the desert
jonah-the-lesson-for-kids.why: God pointed out that Jonah was furious about losing a vine he didn't even grow, yet he wanted God to destroy a city full of people. God's mercy extends to everyone — that's the whole point.

joseph-and-the-angel-for-kids.why: Joseph was a carpenter — a hardworking man who built things with his hands. He was a humble, honest man who God chose to be the earthly father of Jesus.

joseph-and-the-angel-for-kids.q: What did the angel tell Joseph to name the baby, and what does the name mean?
joseph-and-the-angel-for-kids.why: The angel told Joseph to name the baby Jesus, which means "God saves" — because He would save His people from their sins. The name wasn't random — it was a mission statement.

joseph-and-the-angel-for-kids.q: What did Joseph do after the angel appeared to him in a dream?
options: He asked for more time to think about it
He got up and obeyed — he took Mary as his wife
He told the whole town about the dream
joseph-and-the-angel-for-kids.why: Joseph didn't hesitate. Even though obeying meant people would judge him and misunderstand, he got up and did exactly what God told him to do — he took Mary as his wife.

joseph-from-prison-to-palace-for-kids.q: What did Pharaoh's two dreams mean?
options: Egypt would be attacked by an enemy army
Seven years of abundance followed by seven years of terrible famine
Pharaoh needed to build a new palace
The Nile River would dry up forever
joseph-from-prison-to-palace-for-kids.why: God revealed through Joseph that Egypt would experience seven years of incredible harvests, followed by seven years of devastating famine. Joseph's plan to store grain during the good years saved the entire nation.

joseph-from-prison-to-palace-for-kids.q: What position did Pharaoh give Joseph after hearing the interpretation?
options: Second in command of all Egypt
joseph-from-prison-to-palace-for-kids.why: Pharaoh was so impressed with Joseph's wisdom and God-given insight that he made Joseph the second most powerful person in all of Egypt — going from prisoner to prime minister in a single day.

joseph-from-prison-to-palace-for-kids.q: What did Joseph tell his brothers about what they had done to him?
options: "I will never forgive you for what you did"
"You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good"
"You owe me twenty years of your lives"
joseph-from-prison-to-palace-for-kids.why: Instead of revenge, Joseph saw God's hand in everything — even the painful parts. He understood that God used the brothers' evil actions to put Joseph in a position to save many lives, including theirs.

joseph-the-dreamer-for-kids.q: Why were Joseph's brothers so jealous of him?
options: He was the strongest and fastest brother
Their father obviously favored him and gave him a special colorful coat
He had the biggest flock of sheep
He was the oldest and got everything first
joseph-the-dreamer-for-kids.why: Jacob didn't hide that Joseph was his favorite — the colorful coat made it obvious. Combined with Joseph's dreams showing his family bowing to him, the brothers' jealousy turned to hatred.

joseph-the-dreamer-for-kids.q: What did Joseph's brothers do to him?
options: They sent him to live with relatives
They threw him in a pit and then sold him as a slave to traders heading to Egypt
They made him do all the farm work
They burned his coat and sent him away
joseph-the-dreamer-for-kids.why: The brothers threw Joseph into an empty pit, then sold him to passing traders for twenty pieces of silver. They covered it up by putting goat's blood on his coat and telling their father he was dead.

joseph-the-dreamer-for-kids.q: What happened to Joseph in Potiphar's house?
options: He escaped and ran back home
God was with him, everything he did prospered, and he was put in charge of the whole household
He became friends with Pharaoh right away
joseph-the-dreamer-for-kids.why: Even as a slave, Joseph worked with excellence and kept his faith. God blessed everything he did, and Potiphar noticed — putting Joseph in charge of his entire household.

joshua-takes-command-for-kids.q: How many times did God tell Joshua to "be strong and courageous" in Joshua chapter 1?
joshua-takes-command-for-kids.why: God told Joshua to be strong and courageous THREE times! When God repeats something, it means He really wants you to pay attention. He wanted Joshua to deeply understand that courage would be essential for the mission ahead — and that God Himself would be the source of that courage.

joshua-takes-command-for-kids.q: What was God's big promise to Joshua as the new leader?
options: "I will make you rich and famous"
"I will be with you wherever you go"
"You will be even greater than Moses"
joshua-takes-command-for-kids.why: God promised Joshua His presence — "I will be with you wherever you go. I will never leave you or abandon you." God didn't promise an easy road. He promised something even better: that Joshua would never walk that road alone.

joshua-takes-command-for-kids.q: What is the real meaning of courage according to this lesson?
options: Being the strongest and toughest person
Trusting God even when you're afraid
joshua-takes-command-for-kids.why: Courage isn't about never being scared — that's impossible! Real courage means trusting God and doing what He asks even when fear is screaming at you to stop. Joshua was probably terrified to lead an entire nation, but he stepped forward anyway because he trusted God's promise to be with him.

joy-in-all-things-for-kids.q: Where was Paul when he wrote the letter to the Philippians?
options: On a boat sailing across the sea
In a comfortable house in Rome
joy-in-all-things-for-kids.why: Paul wrote Philippians from prison — chained up in a Roman dungeon — yet the letter is the most joyful book in the Bible, with the word "joy" or "rejoice" appearing more than a dozen times.

joy-in-all-things-for-kids.q: What is the difference between joy and happiness?
options: There is no difference — they mean the same thing
Happiness depends on circumstances, but joy depends on knowing Jesus
Joy is for adults and happiness is for kids
joy-in-all-things-for-kids.why: Happiness changes based on what's happening around you, but joy is an anchor — it stays steady because it's rooted in your relationship with Jesus, not your situation.

joy-in-all-things-for-kids.q: What does "I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me" really mean in context?
options: You will win every competition and succeed at everything
God will make sure nothing bad ever happens to you
Christ gives you the strength to endure any situation — even hardship
You can have whatever you want if you pray hard enough
joy-in-all-things-for-kids.why: Paul wrote this verse while talking about being content whether well fed or hungry, in plenty or in want. It means Christ's strength is enough to carry you through any situation — not that life will always be easy.

judah-falls-to-babylon-for-kids.q: Which empire conquered the Southern Kingdom of Judah?
judah-falls-to-babylon-for-kids.why: Babylon, led by King Nebuchadnezzar, conquered Judah and destroyed Jerusalem.

judah-falls-to-babylon-for-kids.q: What was the name of the king who attacked Jerusalem?
judah-falls-to-babylon-for-kids.why: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon led the siege and destruction of Jerusalem.

judah-falls-to-babylon-for-kids.q: What magnificent building was destroyed during the siege?
judah-falls-to-babylon-for-kids.why: Solomon's Temple, the most beautiful building on earth and the place where God's presence dwelled, was torn apart and looted.

let-my-people-go-for-kids.q: How did Pharaoh respond when Moses and Aaron first asked him to let the Israelites go?
options: He agreed but asked for one more week
He refused and made the Israelites' work even harder
He laughed and ignored them completely
He threw Moses and Aaron in prison
let-my-people-go-for-kids.why: Pharaoh not only refused to let the Israelites go, but he punished them by taking away their straw supply while still demanding the same number of bricks -- making their work nearly impossible.

let-my-people-go-for-kids.q: What happened when Aaron threw down his staff in front of Pharaoh?
let-my-people-go-for-kids.why: Aaron's staff turned into a snake as a sign of God's power. When Pharaoh's magicians replicated the trick, Aaron's snake swallowed all of theirs.

let-my-people-go-for-kids.q: Why did things get worse for the Israelites AFTER Moses asked Pharaoh to let them go?
options: Pharaoh made them work harder with less resources
Moses accidentally offended the Egyptian gods
The Israelites refused to work at all
let-my-people-go-for-kids.why: Pharaoh punished the Israelites by requiring them to gather their own straw while still producing the same number of bricks, making their already brutal workload even more impossible.

looking-forward-for-kids.q: Who was the last prophet of the Old Testament?
looking-forward-for-kids.why: Malachi was the final prophet to speak in the Old Testament. His name actually means "my messenger," and he delivered God's last words before centuries of silence.

looking-forward-for-kids.q: What was God's opening message through Malachi?
looking-forward-for-kids.why: Even after all the people's failures and broken promises, God's first words through Malachi were "I have loved you." He started with love, not punishment.

looking-forward-for-kids.q: What did Malachi prophesy God would send before the Lord's coming?
options: A messenger to prepare the way
looking-forward-for-kids.why: Malachi prophesied, "I will send my messenger to prepare the way before Me." This was fulfilled by John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Jesus.

love-is-for-kids.q: What are the first two things Paul says love IS?
love-is-for-kids.why: "Love is patient, love is kind." (1 Corinthians 13:4)

love-is-for-kids.q: What does it mean that love "keeps no record of wrongs"?
options: Love writes down every mistake someone makes
Love forgives and doesn't hold grudges
Love pretends nothing bad ever happened
love-is-for-kids.why: Love forgives. It doesn't keep a running list of every time someone hurt you, waiting to throw it in their face.

love-is-for-kids.q: According to Paul, what happens if you have all knowledge and faith to move mountains, but don't have love?
options: You just need to try harder
love-is-for-kids.why: "If I have a faith that can move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing." (1 Corinthians 13:2)

love-one-another-for-kids.q: How does John define what love is?
options: A warm feeling in your heart
Jesus Christ laid down His life for us
love-one-another-for-kids.why: John's definition of love is the cross. Love is sacrifice — laying down your life for others. That's the standard Jesus set.

love-one-another-for-kids.q: John says we should love "not with words or speech but with ___ and in ___."
love-one-another-for-kids.why: "Let us not love with words or speech but with actions and in truth." Love isn't just something you say — it's something you do.

love-one-another-for-kids.q: What does John say God IS?
love-one-another-for-kids.why: "God is love." Not that God has love or shows love sometimes. Love is His very identity. Everything He does flows from it.

manna-from-heaven-for-kids.q: What did the Israelites complain about in the wilderness?
options: They didn't have enough food and missed Egypt
They wanted to go swimming in the Red Sea
manna-from-heaven-for-kids.why: The Israelites grumbled that they were hungry and actually said they missed the food they had back in Egypt, even though they had been slaves there.

manna-from-heaven-for-kids.q: What happened if someone tried to save extra manna for the next day (except before the Sabbath)?
options: It multiplied into even more manna
manna-from-heaven-for-kids.why: God wanted the people to trust Him daily, so any extra manna saved overnight (except before the Sabbath) would become full of worms and smell terrible.

manna-from-heaven-for-kids.q: How did God provide water for the Israelites at Horeb?
options: It rained for forty days and forty nights
Moses struck a rock with his staff and water poured out
An angel carried water from a river
